S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of difficulties with sustained focus, organization, and follow-through that are developmentally inappropriate and cause functional impairment across settings. Individuals typically show at least six inattentive symptoms for at least six months, with minimal or no prominent hyperactive-impulsive features, and symptoms must have been present since childhood even if they only become impairing under increased demands in adolescence or adulthood. The clinical course is often chronic, with fluctuating severity that becomes more evident when academic, occupational, or multitasking demands increase, such as during school transitions, job promotions, or major life changes. It is distinguished from anxiety, depression, or situational stress by the early onset, pervasiveness across contexts, and a longstanding history of organizational and attention difficulties rather than problems emerging solely in response to a discrete stressor.

patient.personality: Paul is a pragmatic, competitive, and socially energetic outdoors enthusiast who enjoys hands-on work, new tech, and mentoring others in a structured but laid-back style.
patient.stressor: About two and a half years ago, Paul was moved from being a field technician to a crew supervisor-in-training, which suddenly shifted his work from mostly physical tasks to a heavier load of planning, coordinating materials, and keeping track of multiple job sites and schedules. Responsibilities like tracking equipment, managing smart-irrigation controllers, and juggling bids and budgets exposed long-standing attention and organization difficulties that he had previously compensated for with his strong work ethic, physical energy, and hands-on skills. Over the next two years, small but frequent mix-ups with tools, project plans, and paperwork began to strain relationships with his boss and crew, leading to missed opportunities for promotion and growing self-doubt, despite him spending more time trying to “get organized.” After a particularly embarrassing incident where misplaced equipment delayed a major eco-focused project and he was formally written up, Paul became worried that his career trajectory was stalling and agreed to seek a psychiatric evaluation at the urging of his manager and a close friend.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep misplacing tools, paperwork, and my gear at work, and it’s starting to get me in trouble.”

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: In the office or in planning meetings, I’ll start out really focused on the schedule or the new irrigation software, and then ten minutes later I realize my mind has drifted off to thinking about a mower noise or some random idea and I’ve missed half of what was said, even though I’m just sitting there staring at the screen or the foreman talking.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: My boss or one of the guys will be telling me the plan for the day, and I’m looking right at them nodding, but it’s like the words don’t fully land, so a minute later I’m asking, ‘Wait, which site did you say first?’ and they get frustrated because they literally just told me.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: They’ll give me a list—order mulch, confirm the crew for Thursday, update the controller settings, and email the client—and I’ll start it, maybe order the mulch and tweak the controller, then get pulled into something else and completely forget to send the email or confirm the crew until someone’s asking why it isn’t done.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: Anything that means I have to sit still and think hard for a while, like typing up bids or going through spreadsheets to match receipts to jobs, I’ll put off until the last possible second because just opening the laptop feels like this heavy chore and my brain wants to do literally anything else, even stuff I don’t like.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: It’s gotten to the point where almost every week I’m wasting time hunting for something—my keys, the tablet we use for the smart controllers, a set of pruning shears I just had in my hand—and I’ll find it later in some random place, like on top of a sprinkler box or in the wrong truck, with no memory of setting it down there.
